result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): B is better overall. It gives a clear list of what each audience must be able to find, a race-page template and a strong first week that checks the 'runners matter most' guess against analytics and registration data the organizers already have. A invents no data and handles the blog triage and owners well, but it never fully ranks the audiences and is muddled on whether volunteer signup belongs on race pages or its own page. B states a few unmeasured points as near-fact (the 10–15 posts, where support emails come from, how landowners behave online). | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B treats "runners matter most" as an explicit assumption and gives two cheap ways to check it: which pages entrants visit before registering, and asking a few recent entrants how they found the races. It also invents nothing and budgets hours for each step. A gives runners a stronger race-page checklist and a clearer site structure, but asserts things it hasn't measured (landowners rarely browse, most support emails come from missing items). Its check of the runner assumption is buried in a general analytics review. B contradicts itself slightly on whether volunteer signup lives on the race pages or on its own page, but it is the better answer overall.
